_register_note: MIG-111 Phase 0.3 per-build diff-scoped inspection rounds. Every confirmed finding was fixed BEFORE the commit (WA#6); each round re-run after the fix. Round 1: eprintln-only degradation notice. Round 2: compaction proceeding without cross-process exclusion.

confirmed_findings.summary: Both fallback branches of file_guard announce the loss of cross-process exclusion with eprintln! only — the exact channel this subsystem documents as going nowhere in Windows GUI release builds — so the degradation, and every divergence that follows from it, leaves no durable evidence anywhere.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: link_life_restore.rs:404-407 states the rule in this very subsystem: 'NEVER eprintln! a failure a user needs: Windows GUI release builds send stderr nowhere (search.rs documents this in-code)' — and that site therefore calls crate::search::diag_log instead. The new guard breaks that rule at both :286 (lock could not be taken) and :294 (lock file could not be opened). In a release build on Windows the user, the Boss test, and diagnostics.log all see nothing: a Universe on a share with no flock support, or one instance that timed out against another, runs the whole session with the 0.3 protection off while every command returns Ok and every restore/compaction log line reads normal. The 'still held by another process after 5s' string is produced and discarded. This is what turns finding #1 from a detectable degradation into a silent one — and the fix is one line, since `dir` is in hand and crate::search::diag_log(&dir.join("search.db"), msg) is the pattern already used by search.rs:9847 for the walk-append failure in the same module's caller.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source, not inferred. (1) Channel is provably dead: src-tauri/src/main.rs:2 sets `#![cfg_attr(not(debug_assertions), windows_subsystem = \"windows\")]`, and search.rs:1523-1537 documents in-code that eprintln!/println! \"go nowhere even when launched from a terminal\" in that configuration. Both new sites — link_life.rs:286 (lock not takeable) and :294 (lock file not openable) — emit via eprintln! only. (2) No alternate surface: file_guard returns `LedgerGuard { _mutex, os }` with no Result and no field; LoadReport (link_life.rs:88-97) has slots only for skipped_lines / corrupt_renamed_to / refuse_write and nothing for \"exclusion disabled\"; no Tauri event; every command still returns Ok. (3) Both branches reachable: lock_within_budget:270 returns Err IMMEDIATELY for any non-contention error, including a filesystem that does not implement locking (network/SMB share) — that degrades every guard call for the whole session, not a rare window; and the contention branch is live because universe_lock.rs:48-52 states the Phase 0.2 owner lock is non-enforcing (\"two instances could already do this before MIG-111\"), echoed at link_life.rs:435, while link_life_restore.rs:165 runs maybe_compact over the same directory on every boot. (4) The consequence is documented in this very file: link_life.rs:179-184 and :431-435 — a decision lost to the cross-process compact/append race is not merely absent; the fold carries the pre-decision value and WRITES IT BACK, un-retiring a link the user retired or re-imposing a cleared priority, \"while every step logs success.\" (5) The subsystem's own rule is broken: link_life_restore.rs:404-417 states \"NEVER eprintln! a failure a user needs\" — written because this exact swallow produced the Boss's 2026-07-27 \"0 of 34 written\" restore with 33 records unaccounted for — and calls crate::search::diag_log instead. The fix is one line and mechanically correct: `dir` at file_guard IS the .constellation dir (store_dir = conn.path().parent(), link_life.rs:79-85) and diag_log derives diagnostics.log from db_path.parent(), so diag_log(&dir.join(\"search.db\"), &msg) writes the canonical durable sink. I could not refute via guard, reconcile, version gate, unreachability, or self-correction — none exist on this path. Scope correction to the candidate: the class label \"swallowed-write-error\" is imprecise (append/fsync/read_state still surface their own I/O errors) and the degraded state equals pre-0.3 behaviour that main ships today, so this is not itself a new loss path — it is the erasure of the only evidence that a documented loss path has been silently re-opened. That is an observability defect with real data consequences, which holds it below APP-KILLER/HIGH at MED.

confirmed_findings.summary: When the OS lock is not obtained, `file_guard` returns a `LedgerGuard` with `os: None` and the caller proceeds regardless — including the two DESTRUCTIVE operations (`maybe_compact`'s tail rename at :806 and `quarantine`'s live-store rename at :825). Nothing outside `Drop` ever reads `_g.os` (only reference is link_life.rs:235), so the destructive path has no way to know cross-process exclusion is off.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: The Universe sits on an SMB/exFAT/network volume where `try_lock_exclusive` returns a NON-contention error (locking unimplemented). `lock_within_budget` (link_life.rs:270) returns Err immediately, `degraded()` logs one line, `os = None`, and `maybe_compact` (link_life.rs:746) continues into the fold → snapshot persist → `fs::rename(&tail, &dest)` at :806. A second Constellation instance — reachable today, since the module's own comment at :454 records that the Phase 0.2 owner lock is still record-only — is concurrently appending decisions via `record_decision` (search.rs:10824) or `set_review_priority` (review.rs:689). Those appends land in the renamed-aside tail, which is deliberately outside the load path, so they vanish from every future fold. The user's retire / trust / cleared-priority is not merely absent: `link_life_restore::restore` (link_life_restore.rs:239) writes the stale pre-decision value back into `note_links`/`note_meta` on the next boot. Every command returned Ok; the only trace is a diagnostics.log line saying exclusion was off — which never says a record was lost. The availability argument that justifies proceeding for `append` (a lost append is recoverable from the aside copy) does not hold for the rename that CREATES the aside copy: compaction is optional and already has first-class `Refused` / `BelowThreshold` outcomes and re-runs every boot, so refusing costs nothing.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified at source. (1) file_guard (link_life.rs:301-322) yields LedgerGuard{os:None} on both failure branches — lock-file unopenable, and lock_within_budget erroring, which at :270 returns IMMEDIATELY for any non-contention error (the 'filesystem does not implement locking' case the module itself names as a field condition at :284-288 and pins with a test at :1288). (2) The structural claim is exact: grep shows `os` referenced ONLY at :230 (decl) and :235 (Drop) — no caller can branch on it. (3) maybe_compact takes the guard at :746 and proceeds unconditionally through read_state_locked (:756) -> snapshot persist (:799) -> fs::rename(&tail,&dest) (:806), despite its own comment at :742-745 declaring that span 'ONE critical section, and it has to be'. (4) A second instance is reachable TODAY: universe_lock.rs:41-51 and :224-227 state Phase 0.2 is RECORD, do not yet ENFORCE — 'if acquisition fails at activation today, behaviour is unchanged (two instances could already do this)'. (5) Live cross-process appenders confirmed on Tauri command threads: record_decision (search.rs:10824) and set_review_priority (review.rs:689), both append+fsync to Stream::Earned. (6) A record landing between :756 and :806 lands in earned.tail-<stamp>.jsonl, which the module states is deliberately OUTSIDE the load path (:29-30, :668-671); no code ever reads it back. (7) The consequence is an active revert, not mere absence: link_life_restore::restore writes status = e.status.unwrap_or(cur_status) (:318), recorded conf (:307-317) and note priority (:373-385) back into note_links/note_meta, and snapshot_lines emits an explicit status for every link, so the post-compaction snapshot supplies the pre-decision value that overwrites the user's retire/trust/priority. (8) Fully silent: maybe_compact returns Compacted (a success) and link_life_restore.rs:131-138 logs it as one; the only degraded() line says exclusion is off, never that a record was lost. The module's own availability justification at :225-227 ('the aside copy makes a lost append recoverable') is derived for append, where blocking would hang a user command; it is circular for the rename, which is what CREATES the aside copy that nothing reads. Compaction is optional, already has first-class Refused/BelowThreshold outcomes distinctly handled by its only caller (link_life_restore.rs:140-146), and re-runs every boot — so refusing when os.is_none() costs nothing. PARTIALLY REFUTED: the candidate's second destructive site, quarantine's rename at :825, is NOT reachable in production — all three call sites (:1139, :1438, :1843) are inside #[cfg(test)] modules; the finding stands on maybe_compact alone. Severity held at MED, not higher: deep conjunction (2 MB tail ~10,000 records vs the live 6,222 B at :677, two concurrent instances, a lock-unavailable filesystem or exhausted budget, and an append inside the tens-of-ms fold-to-rename window), the bytes physically survive in a kept aside file, and this is not a regression (degraded == pre-0.3 behaviour shipping today) — it is a documented hazard the new guard fails to close on the one path where closing it is free. Fix: return CompactOutcome::Refused when the guard's OS lock was not obtained.
